cells.note: Initial mount + populated render OK (ReportsPanel.tsx:50-58 sort by createdAt, withRecentlyAddedFirst; CardListPanel renders count=cards.length covering both kinds). Empty state OK (ReportsPanel.tsx:84-88). BUT collapsed EMPTY report renders a blank line, not the 'empty' placeholder: ReportCard.tsx:79 passes `makeCompressedSummary(...) || ''`, and EditableCard panel-primitives.tsx:1074 does `compressedSummary ?? <CardEmptyText/>` — `'' ?? x` returns '' (nullish only catches null/undefined). Truncation: makeCompressedSummary slices 80*lines chars (panel-primitives.tsx:183-186) with CSS WebkitLineClamp — sans-class, designed.

Report bodies are editable RichTextField (bodyClass 'sans', card-registry.tsx:411; not BorrowedMainText). Citation atoms render via the SAME Citation extension as main editor (borrowed-schema.ts:150) so click-through DOES select the citation card (citation.ts:269 fires virgil-citation-click). BUT reports-host.tsx:50-64 never reads useCitationDisplayContext() nor passes getCitationDisplayText/onCitationCreated to ReportsPanel — and ReportsPanel doesn't accept them — so citations in report bodies render raw \cite{key} (RichTextField.tsx:205-207,283 fall back to command) and dropped new citations don't register. Every sibling panel (notes/footnotes/archive/citations host) wires these. Compressed report uses flat summary string (sans → useBorrowedCompressed false, panel-primitives.tsx:864) so collapsed bodies lose atom rendering — designed for sans kinds.

Edit body (updateReportContent/updateRequestContent useReports.ts:191-230) and AI-request flag toggle (setRequestAiRequest:232-261 → bridgeCardAiRequestFlag) work. BUT: (1) report-request→report morph orphans the pending ai-requests.json entry — requestToReport (morphs/index.ts:149) drops aiRequest with NO bridge(false) call, convertCard (useReports.ts:267) only applyCardMorph; morph confirm (EditorPane.tsx:875) never mentions the dropped flag [REP-F5-01]. (2) Reports docked panel renders NO Pending-AI-Requests section: reports-host.tsx passes no aiRequests/onUpdate/onDelete to ReportsPanel (Footnotes/Notes do), so a kind:report request (answer-report-request skill) has no inbox row [REP-F5-02]. (3) A user title matching ^Report \d+$ is silently nulled on reload (isAutoTitle, panel-registry.ts:254-258; migrateReportRecord useReports.ts:57-59) [REP-F5-03]. (4) Expanded title input (CardBodyTitle uncontrolled defaultValue, panel-primitives.tsx:552) doesn't re-sync on external title write [REP-F5-04].

findings.subject: reports
findings.symptom: A citation placed inside a Report (or Report Request) body shows the raw LaTeX command \cite{smith2020} instead of the formatted name (e.g. 'Smith 2020'), and a brand-new citation dropped into a report body never appears in the Citations panel / gets no stable id.
findings.suspectedRootCause: reports-host.tsx never consumes the surrounding CitationDisplayProvider: it neither calls useCitationDisplayContext() nor forwards getCitationDisplayText/onCitationCreated to ReportsPanel, and ReportsPanel/buildReportsOmniItems do not accept or thread those props. ReportCard/ReportRequestCard declare the props but receive undefined. RichTextField.refreshCitationDisplay returns the doc unchanged when getCitationDisplayTextRef is undefined (returns doc at the `if (!lookup) return doc` guard), and the drop handler skips onCitationCreated, so citation atoms render `displayText || command` = the bare command and never register. Every other RichTextField-bearing panel host (notes/footnotes/archive/citations) wires these from the same provider.

evidence.note: ReportsPanel mounted with NO getCitationDisplayText/onCitationCreated props and no useCitationDisplayContext() call
sibling notes-host passes getCitationDisplayText/onCitationCreated from useCitationDisplayContext() — the wiring reports-host lacks
ReportCard forwards getCitationDisplayText/onCitationCreated to EditableCard but they arrive undefined (panel never supplies them)
refreshCitationDisplay short-circuits (returns doc unchanged) when the lookup is undefined → stored displayText='' renders the raw command
buildReportsOmniItems renderCard also omits citation-display props → omni report cards have the same raw-\cite defect

reproSteps: Open a paper with a bibliography in the dev doc.
Add a Report card; drop or type a \cite{...} into its body (expanded).
Observe the citation pill shows the raw \cite{key} command rather than the formatted author-year, while the same citation in the main text shows the formatted name.
Drop a brand-new \cite{newkey} into the report body: it never shows up in the Citations panel (no onCitationCreated registration).
findings.suspectedClass: Any panel host that mounts a RichTextField-bearing card but forgets to thread the CitationDisplayProvider values. Reports is the one left-side card panel that missed it; check any future card panel and the float-body builders for the same omission.

findings.subject: reports
findings.symptom: Morphing a Report Request that has its 'AI request' flag on into a Report silently drops the flag AND leaves a stale pending entry in ai-requests.json that can never be cleared through the UI; the confirm dialog never warns the user about either.
findings.suspectedRootCause: report-request → report morph flips kind via requestToReport (drops aiRequest) inside useReports.convertCard, but neither the morph transform nor convertCard calls bridgeCardAiRequestFlag(docId, 'report-request', id, false). The on-disk ai-requests.json request with linkedTo={panel:'reports',cardId} stays 'pending'. The new card is a `report`, which has no aiRequest field and no AI-request checkbox UI, so the user cannot toggle it off; a skill draining the inbox resolves linkedTo.cardId to a `report` (not a request) and is confused. The lossy-morph confirm message (EditorPane.tsx:875) only says 'drops the title and byline' — it never mentions the AI-request flag, and for the request→report direction the message is doubly wrong (a request has no title/byline; the real loss is the flag + orphaned inbox entry).

evidence.note: requestToReport flips kind→report and omits aiRequest entirely — no inbox bridge cleanup
convertCard only calls applyCardMorph inside update(); never bridges the dropped aiRequest flag to ai-requests.json
the only path that removes an inbox entry is a value=false bridge call — which the morph never makes, so the pending request is orphaned
lossy confirm message mentions only title/byline; never the aiRequest flag or the orphaned inbox entry; same message used for both morph directions
report-request declares aiRequest routing {kind:'report',linkPanel:'reports'}; report (line 394) declares none — so the flag has no home post-morph

reproSteps: Add a Report Request, type a body, tick its 'AI request' checkbox (this writes a pending entry to ai-requests.json).
Use the kind chevron to morph it to a Report; confirm the (incomplete) dialog.
Inspect virgil/ai-requests.json: the linked request is still status:'pending' but the card is now a Report with no way to surface or clear it.
Re-morph back to Report Request: a fresh request may be filed, leaving a stale duplicate.
findings.suspectedClass: Any lossy morph that drops an aiRequest flag without bridging it off. note→highlight: noteToHighlight preserves aiRequest (morphs/index.ts:184) so highlight keeps the flag — but highlight's aiRequest routing differs ({kind:'highlight'}) from note's ({kind:'note'}), so the on-disk inbox entry's kind goes stale across that morph too. Check all morph pairs where the two kinds declare different aiRequest routing for inbox drift.

findings.subject: reports
findings.symptom: The docked Reports panel never shows a 'Pending AI Requests' section, unlike Footnotes/Notes/Todos — a standalone or orphaned report AI-request (e.g. one whose request-card was morphed or deleted) is invisible and cannot be edited or dismissed from the panel.
findings.suspectedRootCause: reports-host.tsx does not call useAiRequestsContext() and passes no aiRequests / onUpdateAiRequestText / onDeleteAiRequest to ReportsPanel, and ReportsPanel does not declare or filter aiRequests (no `r.kind === 'report'` filter the way FootnotePanel.tsx:69 / NotesPanel.tsx:83 do). CardListPanel renders the AI-requests section only when given a non-empty aiRequests prop. Yet reports fully participate in the unified inbox (CARD_REGISTRY report-request routes kind:'report'/linkPanel:'reports'; the answer-report-request skill drains kind:'report' entries). Visibility is partly served by the request card's own checkbox, but a request entry with no live card (after REP-F5-01's morph orphan, or after the request card is deleted) has nowhere to render.

evidence.note: ReportsPanel mounted with no aiRequests/onUpdateAiRequestText/onDeleteAiRequest; reports-host never imports useAiRequestsContext
ReportsPanel props omit aiRequests entirely; CardListPanel below it therefore renders no AI-requests section
sibling panels filter aiRequests by kind and pass them to CardListPanel — the section reports lacks
the AI-requests section only appears when a non-empty aiRequests prop is supplied

reproSteps: File a kind:'report' AI request (tick AI-request on a report-request, or have a skill create a virtual reports request).
Delete or morph away the originating report-request card.
Open the Reports panel: there is no Pending-AI-Requests section, so the still-pending request is invisible and unclearable from the UI.
findings.suspectedClass: Polymorphic panels whose request kind lives in the inbox but whose docked host forgot the inbox wiring. Cutter/Revisions hosts should be checked for the same omission (suggestion-kind requests).

findings.subject: reports
findings.symptom: A user who titles a report exactly like the legacy auto-pattern — e.g. 'Report 2', 'Report 14' — loses that title silently on the next document load; it reverts to the empty +T placeholder.
findings.suspectedRootCause: On load, migrateReportRecord nulls any title for which isAutoTitle('report', title) is true. isAutoTitle matches the regex ^Report \d+$ (the kind's CARD_TITLE_LABELS prefix), which cannot distinguish a user-typed 'Report 2' from the legacy generated title that BUG #31 stopped persisting. The auto-title.test.ts even codifies migrateTitle('report','Report 2') === '' as intended, so the lossy behavior is deliberate — but it still destroys a legitimate user title with no warning or recovery.

evidence.note: migrateReportRecord: `title: isAutoTitle('report', r.title) ? r.title-or-'' ` — nulls on the auto pattern at load
isAutoTitle tests ^<Label> \d+$ — 'Report 2' matches regardless of whether the user typed it
test asserts migrateTitle('report','Report 2') === '' as intended behavior — confirms the loss is by design, hence a known-fragile UX hazard, not an accident

reproSteps: Add a Report and set its title to 'Report 2' (e.g. a paper whose section 2 you are reporting on).
Reload the document (close/reopen the paper folder).
The report's title is gone — it shows the +T placeholder.
findings.suspectedClass: Every auto-titling kind: note ('Note 3'), footnote ('Footnote 2'), archive ('Archive Text 1'), todo ('Task 9'), example ('Example 4'). All five share the same isAutoTitle strip-on-load and the same false-positive on a legitimately-typed matching title (auto-title.test.ts:142-163 codifies it for all of them).

findings.subject: reports
findings.symptom: A collapsed Report (or Report Request) with an empty body shows a blank summary line instead of the muted italic 'empty' placeholder that other empty collapsed cards (e.g. Cutter comments) show.
findings.suspectedRootCause: ReportCard/ReportRequestCard build compressedSummary as `makeCompressedSummary(...) || ''` (empty body → ''), and EditableCard renders `{compressedSummary ?? <CardEmptyText/>}`. Because '' is not null/undefined, the nullish-coalescing fallback never fires, so an empty string renders (a blank line) rather than CardEmptyText. CutterCommentCard uses `|| undefined`, which DOES fall through to the placeholder — so the cards disagree.

evidence.note: compressedSummary = makeCompressedSummary(...) || '' → empty body yields '' not undefined
`compressedSummary ?? <CardEmptyText/>` — '' bypasses the fallback, renders a blank line
CutterCommentCard uses `|| undefined` so its empty collapsed card shows the placeholder — proves the intended behavior and the report divergence

reproSteps: Add a Report Request and leave its body empty.
Collapse it (or view it collapsed in the docked panel).
It shows a blank body row; compare to a collapsed empty Cutter comment which shows 'empty'.
findings.suspectedClass: Cards that pass `makeCompressedSummary(...) || ''` instead of `|| undefined`: NoteCard.tsx:95, ArchiveCard.tsx:74, FootnoteCard.tsx:108 & :207, RevisionCommentCard.tsx:75 all share the same blank-instead-of-placeholder behavior; only CutterCommentCard does it the way that surfaces the placeholder.

findings.subject: reports
findings.symptom: When a report's title is changed externally (a skill writes reports.json, or the user edits the title on a different surface) while the expanded card stays mounted, the editable title input keeps showing the old value.
findings.suspectedRootCause: CardBodyTitle (the expanded +T title input) is uncontrolled — it reads `defaultValue={value ?? ''}` once and its only useEffect keys on `[editing]`, never on `value`. There is no instanceKey/remount on value change (EditableCard's instanceKey drives only the RichTextField body). So a prop change to bodyTitle does not propagate into the visible expanded input. The collapsed static title row (panel-primitives.tsx:1040) uses the reactive bodyTitle prop and updates correctly, so the two views can disagree.

evidence.note: CardBodyTitle input uses defaultValue (uncontrolled), no key on value
the only re-sync effect depends on [editing], not [value] — external value changes never refresh the input
the collapsed title row uses the reactive bodyTitle prop, so collapsed vs expanded can desync after an external write

reproSteps: Open a report expanded in the docked panel.
Have a skill (or another open surface) rewrite that report's title in reports.json.
The expanded title input still shows the old title until the card is unmounted/remounted; collapsing shows the new one.
findings.suspectedClass: Shared CardBodyTitle affects every bodyTitle-bearing card: footnotes (FootnoteCard), notes, archive, examples. Any external/cross-surface title write desyncs the expanded input on all of them.
